map.center: Para decir hay: There is + una cosa, There are + muchas. ¡Nunca have!

nodes.title: Preguntas
items: is / are salta delante de there.

items: En el sí, sin contraer: <s>Yes, there's.</s>

error.title: Error común
bad: Have a dog in the park.
good: There is a dog in the park.

mini.es: Completa con there is / there are.
mini.en: Complete with there is / there are.

explain.es: En español decimos hay para todo: hay un gato, hay dos gatos. En inglés hay que elegir: There is para una cosa y There are para muchas. ¡Y nunca traduzcas «hay» con have ni con has!
explain.en: There is + one thing, There are + many things. Never use have to say «hay».

explain.title: 1 · Afirmativa
explain.es: There is va con una cosa (singular) y casi siempre se contrae: There's. There are va con varias cosas (plural): two, three, some, a lot of… There are no se contrae al escribir.
explain.en: There is (There's) + one thing. There are + two or more things.

examples.es: Hay un gato en el sofá.

examples.en: There are three bedrooms in my house.
examples.es: Hay tres dormitorios en mi casa.
Hay una manzana en mi mochila.

explain.title: 2 · Negativa
explain.es: Ponemos not detrás de is / are: There isn't y There aren't. Con plural solemos añadir any. ¡No digas No there is!
explain.en: There isn't + one thing. There aren't any + plural.

examples.en: There isn't a ball in the box.
examples.es: No hay ninguna pelota en la caja.

examples.en: There isn't a cinema in my village.
examples.es: No hay cine en mi pueblo.

explain.title: Truco del dedo
explain.es: Cuenta con los dedos lo que hay: ¿1 dedo? → There is. ¿2 o más? → There are. Y recuerda: si en español dices «hay», en inglés la frase empieza por There.
explain.en: One finger → There is. Two or more → There are. «hay» always starts with There.

explain.title: 3 · Preguntas
explain.es: Para preguntar, is / are salta delante de there, ¡como con to be!

examples.en: Is there a park near your house? — Yes, there is.
examples.es: ¿Hay un parque cerca de tu casa? — Sí.

examples.en: Are there any sweets in the box? — No, there aren't.

explain.title: 4 · Respuestas cortas
head: Pregunta · Question
✅ Sí · Yes
⛔ No
explain.note: En la respuesta corta sí repetimos there, pero el «sí» no se contrae: Yes, there's. → Yes, there is.
explain.note_en: Short answers keep there. Don't contract the yes answer: Yes, there is.

explain.title: SOME y ANY
explain.es: Con plural usamos some (unos, algunos) en las frases afirmativas, y any (ningún, algún) en las negativas y las preguntas. Truco: some = ✅; any = ⛔ y ❓.
explain.en: some in affirmative sentences; any in negatives and questions.

examples.en: There are some books on the table.
examples.es: Hay unos libros en la mesa.

examples.en: There aren't any eggs in the fridge.
examples.es: No hay huevos en la nevera.

explain.title: HOW MANY… ARE THERE?
explain.es: Para preguntar cuántos hay: How many + nombre en plural + are there? Respondemos There are three. Si hay uno: There's one. Y si no hay ninguno: There aren't any.
explain.en: How many + plural noun + are there? → There are… / There's one. / There aren't any.

examples.en: How many children are there in your class? — There are twenty-four.
examples.es: ¿Cuántos niños hay en tu clase? — Hay veinticuatro.

examples.en: How many days are there in a week? — There are seven.
examples.es: ¿Cuántos días hay en una semana? — Hay siete.

examples.en: How many pencils are there in your pencil case? — There's one!
examples.es: ¿Cuántos lápices hay en tu estuche? — ¡Hay uno!

explain.title: ¡Trampa! HAY no es HAVE
explain.es: Como en español «hay» viene del verbo haber, a veces intentamos traducirlo con have o has. ¡Error! have = tener. Para decir que algo existe o está en un sitio, usa siempre there is / there are. ¡Y no te olvides de there!
explain.en: have = tener. To say that something exists or is somewhere, use there is / there are.

cols.head: ✅ Inglés de verdad
items: There's a dog in the park.
There are two beds in my room.
There's a cat on the sofa.

explain.title: THERE IS o IT IS
explain.es: There is / There are presentan algo nuevo (dicen que existe). Después, para describirlo, usamos It is (una cosa) o They are (varias): There's a dog in the garden. It's black.
explain.en: There is introduces something new. Then it is / they are describe it.

Question → Is there…? Are there any…?

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el texto y subraya there is, there are, there isn't y there aren't. Después marca T o F y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the text and underline the there is / there are sentences. Then tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Hi, I'm Mario! My school is in Madrid. It's big and it's got a red door. There are twenty classrooms and there's a big library with a lot of books.
In my classroom there are twenty-four children and one teacher, Miss Brown. There's a whiteboard and there are some computers, but there isn't a TV.
There's a playground with a football pitch, but there isn't a swimming pool. Are there any animals at my school? Yes, there are! There are three fish in our classroom!

items.q: There are twenty classrooms in Mario's school.
There's a TV in Mario's classroom.
There's a swimming pool at the school.
How many children are there in Mario's class?
Are there any animals in Mario's classroom?
items.a: Yes, there are. There are three fish.

items.q: Escribe 2 preguntas para un amigo sobre su casa: Is there…? Are there any…?
